text.p: Three stockbrokers downgraded their recommendations on Dutch brewer Heineken NV on Monday after lower than expected half year profits on Friday.
MeesPierson and Labouchere cut their ratings to "sell" from "hold" and reduced their forecasts of earnings per share while ING Barings lowered its rating to "hold" from "buy".
Heineken on Friday announced a net profit of 297 million guilders for the first half of 1996 and said it expected full year profits to be somewhat lower than those of 1995.
In response, the shares have fallen more than 18 percent.
At 1045 GMT, they were at 299.99 guilders.
MeesPierson analyst Darrel Duthie lowered his forecasts of earnings per share (EPS) to 12.93 from 14.87 for 1996 and to 14.30 from 17.10 for 1997.
John David Roeg of Labouchere cut his EPS estimates to 12.90 from 14.85 for 1996 and to 13.90 from 16.65 for next year.
